classification.difficultyReason: Select candidate rational roots, divide out verified linear factors, and factor the remaining quadratics, repeating the process for the quartic and allowing non-monic factors.

content.prompt: Factorise the following polynomials into a product of linear factors.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^3-2x^2-5x+6$.
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1-2-5+6\\P(1)&=0\end{align*}$$
Thus $x-1$ is a factor. Polynomial division gives
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-1)(x^2-x-6)\\P(x)&=(x-1)(x-3)(x+2).\end{align*}$$

Let $P(x)=x^4-9x^2+4x+12$.
$$\begin{align*}P(-1)&=1-9-4+12\\P(-1)&=0\end{align*}$$
Divide by $x+1$.
$$P(x)=(x+1)(x^3-x^2-8x+12).$$
For $Q(x)=x^3-x^2-8x+12$,
$$\begin{align*}Q(2)&=8-4-16+12\\Q(2)&=0\end{align*}$$
Divide $Q(x)$ by $x-2$ and factorise the quotient.
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+1)(x-2)(x^2+x-6)\\P(x)&=(x+1)(x-2)^2(x+3).\end{align*}$$

Let $P(x)=6x^3-19x^2+x+6$.
$$\begin{align*}P(3)&=162-171+3+6\\P(3)&=0\end{align*}$$
Divide by $x-3$ and factorise the quotient.
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-3)(6x^2-x-2)\\P(x)&=(x-3)(6x^2+3x-4x-2)\\P(x)&=(x-3)\bigl[3x(2x+1)-2(2x+1)\bigr]\\P(x)&=(x-3)(2x+1)(3x-2).\end{align*}$$

Let $P(x)=20x^3-12x^2-23x-6$.
$$\begin{align*}P\left(-\frac12\right)&=-\frac52-3+\frac{23}{2}-6\\P\left(-\frac12\right)&=0\end{align*}$$
Thus $2x+1$ is a factor. Polynomial division gives
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(2x+1)(10x^2-11x-6)\\P(x)&=(2x+1)(10x^2-15x+4x-6)\\P(x)&=(2x+1)\bigl[5x(2x-3)+2(2x-3)\bigr]\\P(x)&=(2x+1)(5x+2)(2x-3).\end{align*}$$
